findings.evidence: the home-office equipment stipend (Eligibility) / the policy applies to one device per category per employee (Restrictions and Exceptions) / You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review. (Terminology Notes)
findings.fix: Pick one term for the purchased object and use it in every section, or add a defined-terms statement establishing the three terms are equivalent.
findings.location: Eligibility, Restrictions and Exceptions, and Terminology Notes
findings.violation: Equipment, device, and stipend item are used across three sections for what appears to be the identical purchased object, with no signal anywhere that the terms are equivalent, so a reader cannot tell whether a stipend item is the purchased device, the request itself, or something else.

findings.evidence: If the position counts as full-time, the stipend can apply. If the employee has completed 90 days of continuous service, the stipend can apply. If the request arrives before the benefit year ends, the stipend can apply. Only once every condition above is met does the home-office equipment stipend become available to the employee.
findings.fix: Open with the governing rule, for example 'The stipend is available only when all of the following conditions are met:', followed by the three conditions as a list.
findings.violation: The governing rule, that all three conditions must hold jointly, is stated only in the fourth sentence; each of the first three sentences reads as though a single condition alone is sufficient, so the reader forms a wrong impression three times before the final sentence corrects it.

findings.evidence: How to Apply: 'Employees start a stipend request in the benefits portal.' ... Request Steps (five headings later): 'Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt.'
findings.fix: Move Request Steps into or immediately after How to Apply.
findings.location: Request Steps section, relative to How to Apply
findings.violation: The actual sequence of steps for filing the request sits five headings after How to Apply, separated by Approval Timeline, Required Documentation, Reimbursement Amounts, and Restrictions and Exceptions, so a reader following How to Apply to start a request has to read through four unrelated sections before finding what the first steps actually are.

findings.evidence: 36-word sentence, 4 subordinate-clause markers: Then, the review takes longer because the manager who normally handles it is traveling; the backup reviewer who covers for absences was not told that the request needs sign-off before the portal releases the confirmation email.
findings.fix: Split the sentence at a subordinate-clause boundary.
findings.violation: The sentence runs to 36 words with 4 subordinate-clause markers, longer than the reader can hold in mind on a single pass.

findings.evidence: The people operations office publishes the reimbursement log each quarter. (Program Overview) / The benefits team publishes the reimbursement log after every open enrollment period. (Overview)
findings.fix: Merge the two sections into one, state a single publisher and a single cadence, and remove the duplicate generic Overview heading.
findings.location: Program Overview (paragraph 1) versus Overview (near end of document)
findings.violation: Two sections make contradicting claims about who publishes the reimbursement log and on what cadence, quarterly versus after open enrollment, with no signal which one governs, so a reader cannot form one consistent belief about how to get an updated log.

findings.evidence: The people operations office publishes the reimbursement log each quarter. A copy of each update goes to the shared benefits folder the same day. Similarly, the IT asset group tracks the stipend budget each quarter. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time.
findings.fix: Split into separate, single-themed sections, or cut the unrelated IT-budget-tracking sentence.
findings.violation: A reader who reads only this section's first and last sentence cannot state what Program Overview is about; the section moves through log-publishing cadence, copy-filing logistics, and unrelated IT budget tracking with nothing connecting the three.

findings.evidence: The people operations office publishes the reimbursement log each quarter. A copy of each update goes to the shared benefits folder the same day. Similarly, the IT asset group tracks the stipend budget each quarter. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time.
findings.fix: Split into two single-topic paragraphs, one on the reimbursement log and its copies, one on the stipend budget, each with a consistent running subject.
findings.violation: Each sentence introduces a new subject (the people operations office, a copy, the IT asset group, staff/the benefits team) with no sentence picking up the subject the one before it established; 'Similarly' promises a parallel the content does not deliver, since budget tracking is not actually similar to log publishing or copy filing.

findings.evidence: The request is reviewed within two business days.
findings.fix: Rewrite the sentence in active voice, naming the actor that performs the action.
findings.violation: The sentence uses a be-verb plus past-participle passive construction in a context where the actor is recoverable and worth naming directly.

findings.evidence: The team logs each request the moment it arrives. The team then routes the request to the correct approver based on department. ... The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out. The finance office also flags any request that repeats within the same quarter.
findings.fix: Cut the internal workflow detail, or recast it as reader-relevant information (for example, state what a $200 threshold means for the employee's own timeline rather than describing finance's internal flagging process).
findings.location: Program Coordination and Review Responsibility sections
findings.violation: These sections narrate internal team routing, logging, and review-threshold mechanics that serve an internal-process reader, not the stipend-requesting employee who is this document's stated audience; the employee has no task that depends on knowing how the benefits team logs or routes a request internally.

findings.evidence: Also, the deposit happens in order to offset costs the employee already paid at this point in time.
findings.fix: Replace the wordy phrase with its plain equivalent (for example, because for due to the fact that).
findings.violation: The sentence uses a wordy construction from the fixed wordy-phrase list that a shorter equivalent would carry with no loss of meaning.

findings.evidence: However, reimbursement is not available without a completed receipt.
findings.fix: Restate the sentence with at most one negation, or recast it as a positive statement.
findings.violation: 2 negation markers from the fixed negation list co-occur in one clause, so the reader has to work out the statement's logical sign before understanding it.

findings.fix: Replace the heading with text specific enough to be found by scanning.
findings.violation: The heading text matches the fixed list of non-specific heading labels, so a reader scanning headings cannot tell whether the section applies to them.
